headline: Cost discipline and new business lift Lear's profitability
summary_short: Lear's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 3.0% y/y to $6.21B as new business and favorable FX offset lower production volumes, while net income climbed 16.7% y/y to $192.8M and diluted EPS rose to $3.79 from $3.06.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.0% y/y (+$179M) to $6.21B as new business (+$94M) and favorable FX (+$106M) offset $171M of lower Lear-platform production in Asia and North America. Gross margin expanded to 7.6% from 7.3% on restructuring benefits and new business, net of price reductions. Seating segment earnings were roughly flat at $286M (6.2% margin); E-Systems earnings rose to $85M (5.4% margin) from $55M on operational restructuring gains and lower restructuring costs. Net income climbed 16.7% y/y to $192.8M ($3.79 diluted EPS), also helped by a smaller share count, despite a slightly higher 20.1% effective tax rate. Cash was $1.0B; Lear repurchased $175M of stock and paid $81M in dividends in H1. Management still targets ~$660M of FY2026 capex.
